purpose: Name recurrent distortions introduced by witness position, credential hierarchy, institutional authority, grief, stigma, and memory.

biases.name: credential hierarchy bias
biases.description: Physician and nurse accounts may be over-weighted while aide, volunteer, family, and deathcare worker knowledge is treated as anecdotal.
biases.guard: record role-specific access and what the role could uniquely see

biases.name: family romance or family blame bias
biases.description: Family accounts may over-idealize, over-blame, or collapse old conflict into the dying scene.
biases.guard: separate observed details from interpretations and preserve missing perspectives

biases.name: official-record finality bias
biases.description: Cause, manner, certificate, and investigation vocabulary can sound complete while excluding bedside texture and contested history.
biases.guard: treat official records as one source type with limited authority

biases.name: worker confession extraction bias
biases.description: Professionals may be asked to narrate traumatic cases for the archive without enough consent, employment safety, or support.
biases.guard: allow anonymity, composite prohibition rules, and withdrawal/edit rights

biases.name: survivor universalization bias
biases.description: Recovered or near-death survivor accounts can be turned into universal maps of dying.
biases.guard: label survivor reports as first-person accounts only and keep nonprophecy language

biases.name: child-material sentimentality bias
biases.description: Children’s words, drawings, and sibling stories can be aestheticized by adults.
biases.guard: highest privacy gate, child-safeguarding review, and no publication without explicit ethical clearance

biases.name: stigma witness bias
biases.description: Overdose, suicide, unhoused, custody, and violent deaths may be narrated through stigma rather than personhood.
biases.guard: safe-messaging, anti-stigma, trauma, and political-opacity review

biases.name: memory-after-grief revision
biases.description: Accounts may change as grief, guilt, dreams, anniversaries, and new information alter the remembered scene.
biases.guard: time-stamp testimony and allow amended accounts without treating amendment as falsification

rule: Bias is not a reason to discard witness accounts; it is a reason to locate them.
